data.gender_notes: Samara is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Samara means 'palm tree'. In the Bible, the city of Samaria is where the Northern Kingdom of Israel is located. The name Samara carries the meaning “Palm tree” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Samara usually hope their child will grow to embody palm tree and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of peace, stability, and nourishment.
data.etymology: Samara belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Palm tree.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Samara total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_hebrew.name: שמרה
in_hebrew.meaning: עץ שמרה, שמורה, קטנה, נשמרה, חגורה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: שמרה (Shomera) היא שם נשים יהודי שמקורו בעברית. השם קשור לעץ שמרה (Psalm 80:10), שהיה עץ חשוב בתקופת העתיקות. השם יכול להתפרש כ"שמורה", "משמרית" או "עץ שמור". בתנ"ך, שמרה היא גם שם של ארבעה אנשים: אבן שמרה (Numbers 25:14), שמרה (1 Chronicles 4:22), שמרה (1 Chronicles 4:30) ושמר (Ezekiel 47:13). בתקופה הביזנטית, שם זה היה נפוץ בקרב הכנסייה הקתולית. בתקופה העות'מאנית, שם זה היה נפוץ בקרב הממלוכים.

in_greek.name: Σαμάρα
in_greek.long_meaning: Σαμάρα (Samara) είναι یک όνομα τού γυναικείου родού που προέρχεται από τη λατινική γλώσσα. Το όνομα σχετίζεται με το σαμάρα (Samarium), ένα χημικό στοιχείο που ανακαλύφθηκε τον 19ο αιώνα. Το όνομα Σαμάρα μπορεί να φανταστεί ως «ποικίλη», «διαφανής» ή «σπάνιμος». Στη Βίβλο, δεν υπάρχει σαφής αναφορά στο όνομα Σαμάρα. Είναι ένα όνομα που έχει λάβει σταδιακά τη μορφή και τη σημασία στην Ευρώπη, ιδιαίτερα στη Γαλλία και στη Γερμανία.

in_latin.name: Samara
in_latin.long_meaning: Samara, nomen femininum, a lingua Latina orta est. Nomen hoc cum Samarium, elementum chemicum, connectio habet. Nomen Samara potest interpretari ut 'variegata', 'transiens', 'rara', 'exigua'. In Biblia, nomen hoc non explicitum est. Nomen hoc Europa, praecipue in Francia et Germania, formam et significatum accepit.

in_english.name: Samara
in_english.long_meaning: Samara is a female given name that originated from Latin. The name is associated with Samarium, a chemical element discovered in the 19th century. Samara can be interpreted as 'varied', 'transient', 'rare', or 'short'. In the Bible, there is no clear reference to the name Samara. It is a name that has gradually taken form and significance in Europe, particularly in France and Germany. In Christian tradition, Samara is associated with qualities of diversity, adaptability, and resilience. The name has gained popularity in modern times, particularly in the context of Christian baby names and biblical inspiration.

data.cultural_impact: Historically, Samaria was the significant cultural center in the ancient world. It was the capital city of the Northern Kingdom of Israel during the 9th to 8th centuries BC. Samaritans developed distinct religious practices and customs that deviated somewhat from those of the southern Kingdom of Judah, leading to cultural tensions and conflict, as recorded in the Bible. The city of Samaria was also later identified with the biblical city of Sychar, where the Samaritan woman at the well encountered Jesus.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian tradition, Samaria holds spiritual significance as a region where Jesus brought salvation and reconciliation to the people. In the story of the Good Samaritan found in Luke 10:25-37, Jesus uses Samaritans as an example of true compassion and love towards one's neighbor, regardless of cultural or ethnic differences. The Samaritan woman at the well, presented in John 4:1-42, is one of the most significant encounters between Jesus and an individual, as Jesus uses the opportunity to reveal himself as the Messiah to her and her community. Overall, the narrative of Samaria in the Bible highlights the importance of love, reconciliation, and understanding among all people, regardless of background or differences.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Samara: Derived from the Hebrew word "shamar" meaning "to guard" or "to keep," Samara symbolizes the protective and nurturing role of a Christian in the spiritual growth and development of others. Spiritually, it encourages one to be a watchful and caring guardian, always ready to offer guidance and support on the journey of faith.

historical_references.reference: Samaria was the capital city of the Northern Kingdom of Israel, known as the Samaritan Kingdom, from the 10th to 5th centuries BCE. It was located in the area north of Jerusalem, in the central part of the Land of Israel.
historical_references.context: Biblical history: the capital city of the Northern Kingdom of Israel

historical_references.reference: During the Roman period (1st century CE), Samaria was a significant center of Jewish opposition to the Roman occupation. The Samaritans, who were descended from the northern Israelites and adhered to their own distinctive religious practices, were frequently in conflict with the Romans and the Jewish community in Jerusalem.
historical_references.context: Roman history: Jewish opposition to Roman rule

On social media platforms such as Instagram and Pinterest, the name Samara is often associated with stunning visuals, from abstract art pieces to breathtaking landscapes. In the spiritual realm, Samara is a name used by some individuals to reflect their personal journey of self-discovery and growth. Blogs, especially those focused on travel and personal development, often feature stories and reflections from people named Samara. Overall, the name Samara carries a sense of creativity, introspection, and adventure.
